title: Governance frameworks
point: NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 and the EU AI Act all ask for evidence that good engineering already produces, so map each expectation to a concrete artefact.
definition: Governance frameworks describe how organisations manage AI risk. NIST AI RMF 1.0 is voluntary guidance, ISO/IEC 42001 is a certifiable management-system standard, and the EU AI Act is a risk-based regulation.

objective.text: Say what kind of instrument each framework is, name the four NIST AI RMF functions, and map framework expectations to artefacts such as a risk register, eval reports and trace logs.

misconceptions.claim: NIST AI RMF is a law that every AI system must comply with.
misconceptions.correction: It is voluntary guidance organised into four functions: Govern, Map, Measure and Manage. Organisations adopt it to structure their risk work, and customers or regulators may refer to it.

misconceptions.claim: Governance is paperwork written after the system ships.
misconceptions.correction: The evidence comes from work done during the build: risk assessments, eval results, logs and oversight design. Reconstructing it afterwards is slower and usually incomplete.

l1: NIST AI RMF 1.0 is voluntary and has four functions. Govern sets policy and roles, Map frames context and risks, Measure assesses them, and Manage treats and monitors them.
ISO/IEC 42001 specifies requirements for an AI management system. An organisation can be audited and certified against it, much as with information-security management standards.

The EU AI Act is risk-based. It prohibits some practices, places obligations on high-risk systems, requires transparency from certain systems such as chatbots, and leaves minimal-risk systems largely alone.
l2: High-risk obligations include risk management, data governance, logging, human oversight and accuracy. The Act also covers general-purpose AI models, and its obligations phase in over several years.
Map each expectation to an artefact you already build. A risk register covers risk management, eval reports cover accuracy, trace logs cover logging and gate design covers human oversight.
Incident records and post-incident reviews show that risks are monitored and managed over time. Link each one to the risk register entries it affects.
l3: Build one evidence pipeline, not one per framework. A single control, such as approval before outbound email, can serve NIST Manage, an ISO/IEC 42001 control and an oversight duty.
Classification drives the work. Whether a system counts as high-risk under the EU AI Act depends on its use, so record your reasoning and have legal counsel confirm it.
Version artefacts with the system. An eval report is evidence only for the model, prompt and tool set it actually tested.
